motivation: Supported exact-point local history suggests a persistent local legacy after focal loss. Test whether the probability of Thalassia re-recording decays with time since loss, which would be consistent with a finite local resilience window rather than only time-invariant site quality.

episode_population.loss_start: same stable point observed in consecutive years t-1 and t; Thalassia present at t-1 and absent at t
episode_population.rationale_for_end_year: t+1 through t+3 can then be evaluated within the monitoring record through 2025
episode_population.exact_annual_observation: risk rows require uninterrupted consensus observations; any missing year stops the episode
episode_population.recurrent_episode_rule: after a return, a later new loss can start a new episode if it again satisfies the frozen start rule

risk_set.duration_1: point absent at loss year t and observed at t+1; outcome is Thalassia present at t+1
risk_set.duration_2: point remained absent through t+1 and is observed at t+2; outcome is Thalassia present at t+2
risk_set.duration_3: point remained absent through t+2 and is observed at t+3; outcome is Thalassia present at t+3

controls: pre-loss run length centered within stable node
predictors.previous_absence_year_other_seagrass: for duration d, use any non-Thalassia seagrass state at t+d-1, before the return outcome is observed

model.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the exact stable meter mark in the current risk year
model.preprocessing: node-center run length before fitting; StandardScaler numeric predictors; OneHot stable node identity

primary_hypothesis.statement: Conditional on remaining absent and re-observed, the exact-point probability of Thalassia re-recording declines as years since focal loss increase.
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: upper bound of 95% stable-node bootstrap interval < 0

secondary_descriptive: observed return hazard at durations 1, 2, and 3
risk rows, nodes, and returns by duration
same duration coefficient without pre-loss run-length control for orientation only

interpretation.supported: Return probability declines with time since exact-point loss after site, local-history, and community-state controls, consistent with a finite recovery/resilience window.
interpretation.unsupported: No robust decline in return probability across the first three years of absence; time-invariant site quality or recurrent detection may better explain the local history signal than a decaying recovery window.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc temporal ecology on an already-opened point-history panel.
A declining return hazard would not prove rhizome survival or physiological reserve decay; observation persistence and unmeasured microsite state remain alternatives.
Return means recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
The duration coefficient is conditional on a point remaining absent and observed up to each risk year; it is not an unconditional population recovery rate.

Do not change the 1–3 year horizon, loss-year range, exact-observation rule, risk-set construction, controls, learner, bootstrap unit, minima, or support threshold after opening the duration endpoint.

implementation_freeze.run_length_centering: Compute pre-loss run length once per unique loss episode and center it by stable-node mean across episodes before expanding each episode into duration-specific risk rows.
implementation_freeze.bootstrap_unit: Stable transect node; all risk rows and all episodes from a sampled node travel together, and duplicate sampled nodes are relabeled to receive separate node fixed effects.
implementation_freeze.previous_other_seagrass: At duration d, use any_seagrass_present from the immediately preceding focal-absent year t+d-1; because Thalassia is absent by risk-set construction, this is non-Thalassia seagrass occupancy.
implementation_freeze.duration_treatment: Numeric linear term taking values 1, 2, 3; no post-outcome binning or nonlinear rescue.
